newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta crop development rated best in the south.
newsitem.headline: Alberta crop development rated best in the south.

text.p: Alberta crop development was rated best in the south with weather and disease problems reported in northern districts, according to Alberta Agriculture's crop report for the week of June 16.
Southern Alberta crops were thriving under an ideal mix of sun and rain.
Central Alberta reported excellent to good soil moisture and crop growth was rated good with some diseases becoming prevalent in the west due to sustained rain.
Northeast Alberta farmers left thousands of acres unseeded due to a very wet spring.
Northwest Alberta was expected to leave 40 to 75 percent of fields unseeded in districts like Athabasca and Thorhild.
Peace River Valley saw limited amounts of rainfall allowing a few more barley and canola acres in the Manning and Beaverlodge areas. Most farmers gave up seeding any more grains or oilseeds.
